headline: Phronix reports reusable agent capabilities that raise task completion in a selected SWE-bench sample
summary: A preprint from researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Illinois Institute of Technology and the University of Tennessee describes Phronix, a harness that turns observed agent interactions into validated tools and skills, reuses them across later tasks, and researches failures under a progress-based retry budget. On 30 selected SWE-bench Lite tasks, the authors report warm-start solve rates of 91%, 87% and 89% for GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6-Sol, compared with baseline rates of 29%, 27% and 65%; their cold-start rates are 67%, 74% and 88%. They report warm-start token use of 0.38–0.40 million per task, versus 1.29–1.47 million for one measured baseline attempt. A single 1000 Genomes workflow case study passes 11 stated correctness checks with Phronix versus 5 of 11 for the baseline. These are author-reported results, not independent reproductions. The comparison charges the baseline a five-attempt budget estimated from one measured attempt while Phronix uses progress-dependent retries, and task order lets learned capabilities transfer within a run.
